newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Alusuisse-Lonza sets eyes on Asia.
newsitem.headline: Alusuisse-Lonza sets eyes on Asia.

text.p: Lonza SpA's chief executive officer said on Monday Asia's contribution to the chemical company's sales was targeted to grow to 30 percent from 10 percent.

"Asia currently contributes about 10 percent of the total sales. Our target is 30 percent in the future," Andrea De Virgiliis said at a news conference, indicating the target could be reached within the next three to four years.
Lonza, the chemical division of Swiss-based Alusuisse-Lonza Holdings, posted sales of US$1.5 billion in 1995.

Feedstocks for the pharmaceutical industry and genetic chemical activity generated 60 percent of the sales, Virgiliis said, adding that feedstocks to the plastics and additives industry accounted for the remaining 40 percent.
Virgiliis was in Singapore to attend the signing ceremony between Lonza and Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) on their new joint-venture purified isophtalic acid (PIA) plant.

Lonza holds an 80 percent stake in the 70,000 tonnes-per-year plant while EDB has the remaining 20 percent. The plant, which is expected to generate US$100 million a year in sales revenue, is targeted for completion by the end of 1998.

The US$125 million Singapore plant, Lonza's second in Asia, is the first step in the company's regional plans, he said. Lonza has a 40 million Swiss franc joint-venture plant in China, producing additives for animal feed.

The new plant would occupy only 20-25 percent of the 75,000 square metre site on the island of Pulau Sakra, southwest of Singapore. Virgiliis said tentative expansion plans range from research and development to biotechnology.
Pulau Sakra is one of seven islands being joined to form Jurong Island, which is planned as an integrated world-class chemical centre.
Lonza's Singapore plant would buy 35,000 tonnes a year of meta-xylene feedstock from UOP Plastics.
Virgiliis said its target market was the South Pacific since use of the product in Singapore was marginal.
The director of EDB's chemicals and biotechnology division, Tan Suan Swee, said Lonza's investment reflected EDB's move to diversify its product range on Jurong island.
Tan said he did not dismiss the possibility that EDB would sell its 20 percent in its joint venture with Lonza.
"After sometime when the project is in good footing, hopefully Lonza will buy back EDB's stake," Tan said.
